The final answer is correct, although the proposed solution's reasoning contains an error.

**Reachability.** The toggle matrix on lamps 1 to 12 is the tridiagonal matrix with all ones on the diagonal and both off-diagonals, because the neighbors of lamps 1 and 12 that lie outside the range (lamp 0) are ignored. Over F₂ its determinant satisfies D_n = D_{n-1} + D_{n-2}, with D_0 = 1 and D_1 = 1. This sequence is periodic with period 3: 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, … Since D_12 = D_0 = 1, the determinant is nonzero. So the matrix is invertible and every one of the 2¹² configurations of lamps 1 to 12 is reachable. The solution's claimed constraint (lamps 11 and 12 must match) is false.

**Maximization.** Lamp 0 is always on, and any subset of the other lamps can be chosen. The maximum of |s| over subsets of 13th roots of unity that include 1 comes from taking a contiguous arc of roots. A block of 7 consecutive roots has |sum| = sin(7π/13)/sin(π/13). Since sin(7π/13) = sin(6π/13), this equals the value for a block of 6. The chosen set {0, 1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 12} is a block of 7 consecutive roots containing lamp 0, so it is achievable and optimal.

**Value.** sin(7π/13)/sin(π/13) = cos(π/26)/sin(π/13) ≈ 0.99271/0.23932 ≈ 4.1481. This matches the given decimal 4.148114905…, and the closed form 1 + 2cos(2π/13) + 2cos(4π/13) + 2cos(6π/13) equals the same quantity.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
